module.network_extended.checks: Describes the network of the IP address (ASN, address block) and lists the other domains hosted on the same address.
module.network_extended.fix:
Review the domains hosted on the same address: spot those that belong to you, those you do not know and those that look suspicious (phishing, illegal content, abandoned sites).
The list comes from passive sources and may contain outdated names: check with `dig +short name A` that each name still points to this address before acting.
Your own names that should not appear here (old sites, staging, internal tools): delete or correct their `A` or `AAAA` record in the DNS zone, or protect the service (authentication, VPN), because a known name is a target.
If suspicious third-party sites share the address: ask the hosting provider to isolate your hosting, or move to a dedicated address (virtual private server, dedicated IP address), especially if it is used to send e-mail, whose reputation suffers from that of its neighbours.
On a server you administer that hosts several sites: separate the sites (distinct system user, container or machine, each updated on its own) so that a compromised site does not contaminate the others.
Compare the ASN, the holder and the address block with the expected hosting provider; a gap needs clarifying with the "BGP and autonomous system" and "IP RDAP registry" modules.
Check the address reputation in DNS blocklists (DNSBL); if it is listed, fix the cause then ask the list operator for removal. Also check its reverse DNS with `dig -x 203.0.113.10 +short` (snippet below).
module.network_extended.title: Extended network
module.network_extended.why: Hosting shared with compromised or malicious sites can harm the address reputation and widens the attack surface.
